content: These references cover topics such as the management and treatment of scabies, molluscum contagiosum, oropharyngeal candidiasis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and other conditions, particularly in the context of HIV-infected patients. 1. Funkhouser ME, Ross A, and Berger TG discussed the management of scabies in patients with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in their 1993 publication in Archives of Dermatology. 2. Golant AK and Levitt JO provided a comprehensive review of the diagnosis and management of scabies, emphasizing the biology of mites, in Pediatric Review (2012). 3. The Group AE published therapeutic guidelines for the treatment of scabies, including the use of antibiotics, in Melbourne, Australia, in 2010. 4. Guerci S et al. highlighted the emergence of neonatal scabies as a sign of changing times in Minerva Pediatrica (2010). 5. Hay RJ explored the lessons learned from animal models in understanding scabies in Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (2004). 6. Hay RJ, Johns NE, and Williams HC analyzed the global burden of skin diseases, focusing on the prevalence and impact of various skin conditions, in Journal of Investigative Dermatology. 7. Janniger CK and Schwartz RA reviewed seborrheic dermatitis in American Family Physician (1995). 8. Larralde M et al. reported on the successful treatment of crusted scabies with ivermectin in four pediatric patients in Pediatric Dermatology (1999). 9. Leppard B and Naburi AE described the use of ivermectin to control a scabies outbreak in a prison setting in British Journal of Dermatology (2000). 10. Ly F et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial comparing ivermectin and benzyl benzoate for the treatment of scabies in Dakar, Senegal, published in Bulletin of the World Health Organization (2009). 11. Meinking TL et al. evaluated the efficacy of ivermectin in treating scabies in New England Journal of Medicine (1995). 12. Mounsey KE and McCarthy JS reviewed the treatment and control strategies for scabies in Current Opinion in Infectious Diseases (2013). 13. Mytton OT et al. assessed the safety of benzyl benzoate lotion and permethrin during pregnancy in a retrospective matched cohort study published in BJOG (2007). 14. Nofal A reported variable responses to oral ivermectin in treating crusted scabies in eight Egyptian patients in Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (2009). 15. Pacque MC et al. examined the community-based treatment of onchocerciasis with ivermectin, focusing on acceptability and early adverse reactions, in Bulletin of the World Health Organization (1989). 16. Patton LL et al. studied the prevalence and classification of HIV-associated oral lesions in Oral Diseases (2002). 17. Portu JJ et al. described atypical scabies presentations in HIV-positive patients in Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology (1996). 18. Quarterman MJ and Lesher JL documented the treatment of neonatal scabies with permethrin 5% cream in Pediatric Dermatology (1994). 19. Sharquie KE et al. investigated the use of 8% and 10% topical sulfur ointments in different application regimens for scabies treatment in Journal of Drugs in Dermatology (2012). 20. Strong M and Johnstone P reviewed interventions for treating scabies in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews (2007). 21. Subramaniam S et al. presented a case of a papulopustular, vesicular, crusted rash in a 4-week-old neonate in Pediatric Emergency Care (2013). 22. Sullivan JR et al. reported the successful use of ivermectin in treating endemic scabies in a nursing home in Australian Journal of Dermatology (1997). 23. Vekic DA et al. conducted a systematic review of scabies treatment in HIV-infected individuals, which is currently in preparation. 24. Walton SF and Currie BJ discussed the challenges in diagnosing scabies as a global disease affecting both human and animal populations in Clinical Microbiology Reviews (2007). 25. The World Health Organization (WHO) published guidelines on the epidemiology and management of common skin diseases in children in developing countries in 2005. 26. Calista D et al. reported the resolution of disseminated molluscum contagiosum with highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) in AIDS patients in European Journal of Dermatology (1999). 27. Drain K et al. described recurrent giant molluscum contagiosum as part of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) following antiretroviral therapy initiation in an HIV-infected South African male in International Journal of STD & AIDS. 28. Hicks CB et al. documented the resolution of intractable molluscum contagiosum in an HIV-infected patient after initiating antiretroviral therapy with ritonavir in Clinical Infectious Diseases (1997). 29. Horn CK et al. reported the resolution of severe molluscum contagiosum with effective antiretroviral therapy in British Journal of Dermatology (1998). 30. Husak R et al. examined the clinical manifestations and prognostic significance of molluscum contagiosum in HIV patients in Hautarzt (1997). 31. Leahy AB et al. described eyelid lesions as the initial manifestation of molluscum contagiosum in AIDS in American Journal of Ophthalmology (1997). 32. Liota E et al. evaluated imiquimod therapy for molluscum contagiosum in Journal of Cutaneous Medicine and Surgery (2000). 33. Maurer T et al. studied the impact of HAART on dermatologic diseases in HIV-1-infected women in Clinical Infectious Diseases (2004). 34. WHO published consolidated guidelines on general HIV care and antiretroviral drug use for treatment and prevention in 2013. 35. Yang YL et al. investigated the effect of prolonged HAART on oral colonization with Candida and candidiasis in BMC Infectious Diseases (2006). 36. Harr T and French LE reviewed Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis in Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases (2010). 37. Léauté-Labrèze C et al. discussed the diagnosis, classification, and management of erythema multiforme and Stevens-Johnson syndrome in Archives of Disease in Childhood (2000). 38. Rani M and Maurer T are preparing a systematic review on the treatment of drug-induced Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis in HIV patients. 39. WHO published guidelines on surgical care at the district hospital in 2003.
